The goal of integration by parts is to go from an integral 1u dy that we don’t see how to evaluate to an integral 1y du that we can evaluate. Generally, you choose dy first to be as much of the integrand, including dx, as you can readily integrate; u is the leftover part. When finding y from dy, any antiderivative will work and we usually pick the simplest one; no arbitrary constant of integration is needed in y because it would simply cancel out of the right-hand side of Equation (2).
